intro:
Use a field around a form control to give it a label, a line of help and an error message, all tied to the control for screen readers without ids passed by hand.

Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Radio Group and Switch all work inside a field. `Field.Label` is a [Label](/docs/web/components/label), so `required`, `optional` and the label's parts work in it.
usage:
<Field name="email">
  <Field.Label>Work email</Field.Label>
  <Input type="email" required />
  <Field.Description>We send the receipt here.</Field.Description>
  <Field.Error match="valueMissing">Enter an email address.</Field.Error>
</Field>

examples.title: Validation
examples.description: The browser's checks (`required`, `type="email"`, `minLength`) run when the control is left, not on every key. `Field.Error` with `match` shows a message for one of them. While an error shows, the description is hidden.

examples.title: An error from the server
examples.description: Set `invalid` for an error the browser cannot find, such as a name already taken. A `Field.Error` with no `match` shows whenever the field is invalid.

examples.title: Other controls
examples.description: A Select, a Textarea and a Switch, each in a field. For a switch, put it in the label's `Label.Action`.

notes:
### Field.Error

With no children, it shows the browser's own message for the failed check.

### Disabled

`disabled` on the field disables its control and fades its label.
